svg.title: Sid Meier's Civilization 64bit: recovery coverage of civ.exe
svg.desc: All 1,065 functions of civ.exe recovered to C; all 699 live game functions ported into civ64 (91.5% of the code bytes) and verified; 3.6% run-time library replaced by rt; 4.9% dead code not ported.
svg.text: How much of the Windows 3.1 civ.exe was recovered: every function to C, every live function ported or replaced
Where every byte of civ.exe went (416,385 code bytes)
Borland runtime, replaced by rt: 155 functions, 14,993 bytes (3.6%)
Dead code, not ported: 211 functions, 20,456 bytes (4.9%)
In civ.exe but never run: 178 functions have no reference at all, and 33 are reached only from those.
51 unused run-time library routines, 68 empty or constant stubs and 92 unused game routines (diagnostics, Mac-port leftovers,
unused helpers). Recovered to C and documented, but not ported because nothing can call them.
Every function, in address order 1000:0000 to 1220:1936 (width = size; grey = dead code; each strip is 33.9 KB)
Sources: claude/docs/db/functions.json, claude/port/docs/TRACE.md and the port's records; generated by claude/tools/recovery_coverage.py
